newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended moderately higher Monday, buoyed by commission house and light arbitrage buying amid constructive CFTC data, dealers said.
But with only 2,945 lots changing hands on the day, traders said activity was unimpressive.
"The CFTC report was probably bullish, but I do not think the market reacted that much to it," one trader said. "It really a quiet day."
Spot March futures ended up $9 at $1,323 a tonne after ranging from $1,326 to $1,313. Most-active May rose $11 to $1,352, while the outer months finished $3 to $12 higher.
Cocoa prices spent the bulk of the session in positive territory after CFTC data showed speculators were net short by 1,658 contracts to Jan. 28.
Traders said a weak dollar against Sterling was supportive because arbitrage favored dollar-denominated CSCE cocoa.

Technically, traders said the March contract would need to get through $1,343-$1,345 to attract substantial buying interest. On the downside, $1,307-$1,309 was likely to provide strong support, they said.

In fundamental news, French chocolate manufacturer Cantalou said it was planning to build a cocoa bean processing plant in Ivory Coast with a capacity of 60,000 tonnes a year. The news comes in line with an increasing shift in processing from consumer countries to origins. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212-859-1640))
